From my experience, metal is the most isolating genre. I remember reading an article which made this claim based on Spotify data--the average metal fan listens more exclusively to metal than the average hip-hop fan does to hip-hop. or the average classical fan does to classical. And it seems it works the other way too--non-metalheads tend to forget the genre exists. I am a music major at a college which attracts a lot of diverse interests, and I could count on one hand the number of times I've heard a contemporary metal band or musician being discussed. It's just not on anyone's radar. Do you agree, and if so, why do you think this divide is so strong? Also, what advice/recommendations would you provide to a music major such as myself?

I tend to agree. Classic rock is another genre I listen to as well as EDM........ but my go to music is ALWAYS metal. When I get into my car the first thing I think to do for my commute is put on the latest metal album I got. Everything else just doesn't seem to exist unless someone reminds me of it.

I also feel like I have become so familiar with the loud bombastic sounds of metal that I can easily put on Arch Enemy or early Hypocrisy while I do my morning routine before work. Doesn't matter the time of day.

If you are looking for advice to helping understand what is so appealing I would recommend this:

Start with something very basic. Something that is to formula. For example this song from the new Cain's Offering album https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VECI3keYKug (I Will Build You A Rome) or Unbreakable by Stratovarius https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7rTvUiJZVgA Both songs have the same singer BTW. Now I always use power metal to introduce someone to metal because it seems to be the "easiest" genre to get into. Mostly due to the fact that you can completely understand what the vocalist is singing and most people who casually listen to music prefer this. From there I will usually introduce something that still has the musical style of power metal but more growling vocals that are a little harder to understand. In this sense I took Children of Bodom's Hatebreeder https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-InrrfJww9Q . Being by far my favorite band, Alexi (the singer and lead guitarist) spent most his time writing more neo-classical solos and interludes on this album. This one song in particular hooks me every time. Love it.

From there you can venture more forward into the realm of metal and eventually hitting death, doom, black, etc. Each genre of metal has its reasoning as to why it sounds the way it is. Just quickly: death metal was "invented" to lash back to pop music as heard on the radio. Every instrument being the complete opposite. Bass cannot be heard, drumming is fast, guitars are extremely distorted and the vocals are growled instead of sung. Bands like Amon Amarth have a more "polished" sound www.youtube.com/watch?v=CpAcxbtXUgQ that isn't always accepted by fans who consider themselves (or others consider) to be "elitists". Though a band like Amon Amarth is accepted in North America where you will find the majority of fans actually listening to bands that are not even considered to be metal by fans in Europe.

Seriously, the genre of metal is extremely deep and can be twisting and confusing. I've been a metal fan since around 2002 and after years of tape trading, recording demos, just partaking in listening, and running underground labels... I am still learning new things almost daily about this genre.

I've gotten into metal just within the past year, and I've found that now a lot of other genres seem to lack the emotional depth that metal has (as I mentioned in my other comment).

As for recommendations, what got me into metal was August Burns Red. Some would argue that they're not really metal and they're just metalcore, but they're a great place to start. Unlike a lot of generic metalcore bands, their lead guitar is actually really technical and they bring a lot of melodies along with their heavy breakdowns. They just put out a new album at the end of June and I really like Majoring in the Minors off that album. As a music major, if you're looking to get really musically complex, you can look at progressive metal bands like Between the Buried and Me. Here's an older song of theirs that I really like: Alaska.

Hope this helps! Also LurkSubwalker's post is really good, so I'm not trying to overshadow that, just trying to throw in my two cents.

I have a really hard time articulating into words how I feel about the music that catches my attention, because even within genres I like, I find myself being really picky and arbitrary. The thing that appeals to me most in music is something beautiful that speaks to ugliness (Jill Tracy's "Anything at All" or "Torture" are probably good examples of this, maybe "Fearful" or "To Kill a King" by Hungry Lucy), or something ugly that speaks to beauty in some fashion (A lot of Ihsahn songs might exemplify this, maybe?). Since those are both kind of rare, I'll often default to something that gets close to that but doesn't quite hit it. Consequently I listen to a lot of stuff like Eluveitie and so on, but also I see music as a cathartic, so certain kinds of ragey music (not necessarily in terms of content--I might take a less talented band over a more technically adept one if the "better" band can't grab me by the guts and rattle the cage of the animal inside) actually makes me feel more upbeat, which is why I like stuff like Ihsahn and Immortal. That use of music as a sort of emotional purgative or a vicarious experience dictates to some degree what I find appealing.
